- [ ] **Step 18: Write the implementation (`.github/workflows/install-probes.yml`)**

The workflow follows `bundle` (T12) with `workflow_run` and downloads that run's artifacts with `actions/download-artifact` (`run-id` plus `github-token`; hence `actions: read`). It checks out the commit that was bundled (`workflow_run.head_sha`) so the scripts match the packages. The action SHAs are the ones `bundle.yml` pins. Runner images match `bundle.yml` (`windows-2022`, `macos-15`, `ubuntu-22.04`). Each job runs the script's self-test first, then the probe, and uploads the evidence directory even on failure. The Fedora job is a plain `docker run` of `fedora:40` (as in T12's `fedora-rpm` job) with `--env CI=true`, because the pinned fixture refuses to run without it; the script installs Xvfb and the session-bus tools inside the container and re-executes under `dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a`.

```yaml
name: install-probes

# Installed-package floor probes (spec §9.4, §12.2, §13 "Scripts-enabled matrix", §14 M1 spike):
# every shipped package is installed fresh from the artifacts of the `bundle` workflow (T12), the
# installed app is started with `--background` against a CI pinned-paths fixture, and its
# `event=sandbox_probe` line in <data>/logs/diag.log must say `floor=met`.
#
#   windows-per-user      NSIS  setup.exe /S /CurrentUser   ACEs by the installer hook, re-apply, WER
#   windows-per-machine   NSIS  setup.exe /S /AllUsers      ACEs by the installer hook, WER
#   macos-arm64           dmg -> /Applications, ad-hoc signed, hardened runtime
#   macos-x86_64-rosetta  dmg (x86_64) -> /Applications, runs translated on the arm64 runner
#   ubuntu-deb            apt install of the .deb
#   ubuntu-appimage       the AppImage through the FUSE runtime
#   fedora-rpm            dnf install of the .rpm in a fedora:40 container, tray_host=missing
#
# The run of a script with "Allow scripts with degraded confinement" off is M8's half of the
# matrix; the upgrade drain and the uninstall checks are M10.
#
# workflow_run only fires for the copy of this file on the default branch. Before it is merged,
# start it by hand: gh workflow run install-probes.yml --ref <branch> -f bundle_run_id=<id of a
# successful bundle run>.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [bundle]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bundle_run_id:
        description: "Id of a successful run of the bundle workflow whose bundle-* artifacts are probed"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  windows-per-user:
    name: windows-per-user (NSIS /CurrentUser on windows-2022)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: windows-2022
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./ci/install-probe-windows.ps1 -SelfTest

      - name: Install per user, start the app, read the sandbox_probe line, re-apply a removed ACE
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}\install-probe-evidence
        run: ./ci/install-probe-windows.ps1 -Mode CurrentUser -InstallerDir dist

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-windows-per-user
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}\install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  windows-per-machine:
    name: windows-per-machine (NSIS /AllUsers on windows-2022)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: windows-2022
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./ci/install-probe-windows.ps1 -SelfTest

      - name: Install per machine, start the app, read the sandbox_probe line
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}\install-probe-evidence
        run: ./ci/install-probe-windows.ps1 -Mode AllUsers -InstallerDir dist

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-windows-per-machine
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}\install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  macos-arm64:
    name: macos-arm64 (dmg on macos-15)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-aarch64-apple-darwin
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-aarch64-apple-darwin
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # /bin/bash is the 3.2 that ships with macOS; the scripts are written for it.
      - name: Self-test the probe script
        run: /bin/bash ci/install-probe-macos.sh --self-test

      - name: Install from the dmg, start the app, read the sandbox_probe line
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
        run: /bin/bash ci/install-probe-macos.sh dist arm64

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-macos-arm64
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  macos-x86_64-rosetta:
    name: macos-x86_64-rosetta (x86_64 dmg under Rosetta 2 on macos-15)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Rosetta 2 and fail loudly if it does not work (§15 V32)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          machine="$(uname -m)"
          if [ "$machine" != "arm64" ]; then
            echo "::error::runner hardware is $machine, expected arm64"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! sudo softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license; then
            echo "::error::softwareupdate could not install Rosetta 2"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true; then
            echo "::error::Rosetta 2 is installed but cannot run x86_64 code"
            exit 1
          fi
          translated="$(arch -x86_64 /usr/sbin/sysctl -n sysctl.proc_translated)"
          echo "sysctl.proc_translated under arch -x86_64: $translated"
          if [ "$translated" != "1" ]; then
            echo "::error::x86_64 process is not translated by Rosetta"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-apple-darwin
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-apple-darwin
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        run: /bin/bash ci/install-probe-macos.sh --self-test

      - name: Install from the dmg, start the translated app, read the sandbox_probe line
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
        run: /bin/bash ci/install-probe-macos.sh dist x86_64

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-macos-x86_64-rosetta
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  ubuntu-deb:
    name: ubuntu-deb (apt install on ubuntu-22.04)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        run: bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh --self-test

      - name: Install the deb, start the app under xvfb + dbus-run-session, read the sandbox_probe line
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
        run: bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh deb dist

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-ubuntu-deb
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  ubuntu-appimage:
    name: ubuntu-appimage (FUSE runtime on ubuntu-22.04)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        run: bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh --self-test

      - name: Run the AppImage under xvfb + dbus-run-session, read the sandbox_probe line
        env:
          INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
        run: bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh appimage dist

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-ubuntu-appimage
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  fedora-rpm:
    name: fedora-rpm (dnf install in a fedora:40 container)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the commit that was bundled
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || inputs.bundle_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Self-test the probe script
        run: bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh --self-test

      # A plain `docker run`, like the bundle workflow's fedora-rpm job: the stock fedora:40 image
      # has no git or tar for the checkout and cache actions. CI=true is passed on because
      # ci/pinned-fixture.sh refuses to run without it. The script installs xvfb and the session
      # bus tools itself and re-executes under `dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a`.
      - name: Install the rpm on Fedora 40, start the app, read the sandbox_probe line
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          evidence="$RUNNER_TEMP/install-probe-evidence"
          mkdir -p "$evidence"
          docker run --rm \
            --env CI=true \
            --env INSTALL_PROBE_EVIDENCE=/evidence \
            --volume "$PWD:/work:ro" \
            --volume "$evidence:/evidence" \
            --workdir /work \
            fedora:40 \
            bash ci/install-probe-linux.sh rpm dist

      - name: Upload the evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: install-probe-fedora-rpm
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/install-probe-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14
```

Expected: PASS. All seven jobs are green. The last line of each probe step:

| Job | Last line of the probe step |
|---|---|
| `windows-per-user` | `OK: CurrentUser install, floor=met, ACEs granted by the installer, WER exclusions set` |
| `windows-per-machine` | `OK: AllUsers install, floor=met, ACEs granted by the installer, WER exclusions set` |
| `macos-arm64` | `OK: arm64 app installed from the dmg: hardened runtime, floor=met (task_for_pid on the app blocked), the app is still alive` |

Then download the evidence for T22: `gh run download <install-probes run id> --dir evidence/install-probes`. From each `install-probe-<job>` directory record into `docs/m1/go-no-go.md` (T22): the full `sandbox_probe` line (`probe-line.txt`, or `probe_line_1` in the Windows `evidence.json`), `extra_layers` (Landlock ABI presence on the Ubuntu and Fedora runners), the Windows `install_dir` and `install_dir_form`, `icacls-worker.txt`, and `worker-paths.txt` (AppImage). If a job is red, the log dump in its step output names the failing probe in `failed=`; a red `windows-per-user` re-apply step with `ace=present` instead of `ace=reapplied` means T19's `check_aces` does not treat a missing S-1-15-2-2 ACE as missing (see the open items below).

Notes and open items (also returned to the plan author):
- Per-user install dir: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Atlas Duck` was observed, not `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas Duck`. The probe asserts the invariant (never the data dir) and records the form.
- T19 contract: the re-apply assertion needs `ensure_aces`/`check_aces` to treat a worker that lacks only the S-1-15-2-2 ACE as `Missing` (re-grant, `ace=reapplied`). If T19 models that case as `AllPresent { lpac_ready: false }`, the per-user re-apply step fails with `ace=present` and one of the two tasks must change; the spec (§9.4: "re-applies missing ones") supports re-applying.
- WER: the check is registry-level (value present under HKCU `ExcludedApplications`). That a crash then produces no dump is not tested; M1 has no crash trigger for the worker.
- macOS: the `sandbox_probe` line does not list per-probe records, so TaskForPid being Blocked is inferred from `floor=met` and `failed=none` (TaskForPid is a floor probe). A per-record log field would be a T20 change; nothing here needs it.
- The `ubuntu-appimage` job installs WebKitGTK and appindicator from apt (the AppImage may rely on them); an AppImage on a bare host is not tested.
- The Fedora container shares the runner's kernel; Docker's default seccomp profile may hide Landlock (`extra_layers` then shows it off, which is reported, not a floor failure); the temp data dir lies on overlayfs, which T06's locality check must classify as local (T06's `f_type` list decides; unverified here).
- Not M1: the NSIS upgrade drain, the "delete app data" option and the uninstall checks (M10); a successful script run with degraded confinement off (M8).

---

### Task 22: Record the go/no-go per OS and run the M1 exit criterion

**Goal:** Write the spike outcome per OS and install mode into a reviewed document with the §15 verify-item findings M1 produced. Check it mechanically and confirm the M1 exit criterion: every M1 CI workflow green on the recorded commit, and the §9.4 probes passing per OS.

**Files:**
- Create: `app/src-tauri/tests/probe_evidence.rs` (plan addition, see "Plan decisions")
- Create: `ci/check-go-no-go.mjs`
- Create: `ci/check-go-no-go.test.mjs`
- Create: `docs/m1/go-no-go.md`
- Modify: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (two steps in job `rust`, one step in job `rust-macos-x86_64-rosetta`, new job `probe-evidence-fedora`, and the final step `M1 go/no-go record (T22)` in job `rust`)
- Test: `ci/check-go-no-go.test.mjs`, `app/src-tauri/tests/probe_evidence.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - CI results and logs of T02, T05, T06, T09, T11, T12, T14, T16 to T21. Names this task reads or relies on:
    - T20 `atlas_duck_app_lib::sandbox_probe::{run_startup_probe(install_dir: &Path, app_pid: u32, profile: &Path) -> (ProbeReport, Option<AceEnsure>), sandbox_worker_path(install_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf}`. `run_startup_probe` already does the Windows ACE ensure and the Linux `ProcTaskStatusHook`, so the new test does not touch spawners.
    - T15 `atlas_duck_sandbox_host::probe::{ProbeReport { worker_version, engine_version, identity, confinement, threads, records: Vec<ProbeRecord { probe, outcome, evidence }>, floor, extra_layers }}`, all `Debug`. T15 runs one worker per floor probe plus one each for `EngineSelfTest` and `EnvNames`, so a report has 9 records on Windows, 8 on macOS and 10 on Linux.
    - T13 `ProbeId` serde `snake_case` names and the per-OS floor lists (Linux 8, macOS 6, Windows 7 probes).
    - T09 `atlas_duck_app_lib::startup::crash::set_non_dumpable() -> std::io::Result<()>` (Linux; `Unsupported` elsewhere).
    - T02 `ci.yml`: job `rust` (steps `Workspace dependency rule (§2.2)` and `CI script tests`), job `rust-macos-x86_64-rosetta` (step `Test x86_64-apple-darwin (test binaries run under Rosetta)`), job `supply-chain`, `defaults.run.shell: bash`.
    - T03 job `ui`. T05 step `Record host name sources and pinned-file base folders (§15 V28)`. T06 jobs `locality-mounts (ubuntu-22.04)` and `locality-mounts (windows-2022)` with their `V29 ...` log lines. T12 `bundle.yml` jobs `bundle-windows`, `bundle-macos-arm64`, `bundle-macos-x86_64`, `bundle-linux`, `fedora-rpm`, `appimage-smoke`. T17 `ci/fedora-probes.sh`. T21 `install-probes.yml` jobs `windows-per-user`, `windows-per-machine`, `macos-arm64`, `macos-x86_64-rosetta`, `ubuntu-deb`, `ubuntu-appimage`, `fedora-rpm` and the `event=sandbox_probe floor=<met|not_met> failed=... extra_layers=... engine_version=... worker_version=... ace=...` line (T20).
    - T01/T02 `node --test "ci/*.test.mjs"` (picks up the new test file by its name).
- Produces:
  - `node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs <doc> [--verify-git] [--verify-runs]`: exit 0 = valid (prints `ok: <doc> (6 targets...)`), exit 1 = violations (one per line on stdout), exit 2 = usage error or unreadable file or a failing `gh`/`git` call. Exports `check(text) -> string[]`, `verifyRuns(text, fetchJson) -> string[]`, `verifyGit(text, git) -> string[]` and the constants `FLOOR_PROBES`, `TARGET_OS`, `REQUIRED_FINDINGS`, `REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS`, `REQUIRED_OPEN_ITEMS`, `ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD`.
  - `docs/m1/go-no-go.md`, one `### <target>` row per target in `windows-per-user`, `windows-per-machine`, `macos-arm64`, `macos-x86_64-rosetta`, `ubuntu-22.04`, `fedora-40`. Each row has `commit` (40 hex), `run` (https URL of its install-probes job), `verdict` (`GO` or `NO-GO`), `reason` (required for NO-GO), `extra layers`, `evidence source`, one or more `install line`, on Linux `threads`, and the floor-probe table (outcome and evidence per probe). A `## Findings` section has one entry per V02, G-5, V03, V09, V10, V11, V12, V14, V28, V29, V30, V32, V33. A `## Open for later milestones` section lists what stays open.
  - Test `app/src-tauri/tests/probe_evidence.rs` (`print_probe_evidence`): prints `PROBE_EVIDENCE ...` lines (grammar below). Env override `ATLAS_DUCK_SANDBOX_BIN`.
  - `ci.yml`: step `Probe evidence (§9.4, go/no-go record)` and step `Show the printed probe-test evidence (V09, V10, V11 go/no-go record)` in job `rust` (every leg), step `Probe evidence (§9.4, go/no-go record)` in job `rust-macos-x86_64-rosetta`, job `probe-evidence-fedora`, step `M1 go/no-go record (T22)` in job `rust`. Log lines prefixed `RUNNER_FACT` and `PROBE_EVIDENCE`.

**Spec:** §14 M1 ("Ends with a recorded go/no-go per OS"), §9.4 (floor and probes; "If the floor cannot be applied and verified, scripts are disabled"; "Missing extra layers ... are reported but do not disable scripts"), §15 (verify items V02, V03, V09 to V12, V14, V28 to V30, V32, V33), §13 CI row (scripts-enabled matrix, Fedora container, Rosetta), §2.5 (crash artifacts, memory-read self-test never blocks startup).

**Plan decisions (the spec is silent or leaves it open; flag each to the user):**
- **Where the record lives (gap G2):** `docs/m1/go-no-go.md`. The spec fixes neither place nor format. The format is the plan's and the checker enforces it.
- **What a NO-GO means:** the spec fixes only the runtime consequence (floor not met: scripts disabled, `failed`, exit 8, `error.code = sandbox_unavailable`, unless the user enables "Allow scripts with degraded confinement"). What a NO-GO means for the project (for example research A1's suggestion to try the `-gnu` Windows toolchain if MSVC fails) is not decided here. The document says so, and Step 11 hands any NO-GO to the user.
- **The checker and the exit criterion are separate.** A NO-GO row with a reason is a valid record and passes the static check. The exit criterion (every M1 workflow green on the recorded commit, all six rows GO) is `--verify-git --verify-runs` plus the verdicts. If any row is NO-GO, M1's "the §9.4 probes pass per OS" is not met: report that to the user and stop.
- **V numbers.** The spec's §15 has no numbers. The plan numbers its bullets from V01 in order (V02 Eval, V03 MSVC, V09 AppContainer, V10 `sandbox_init`, V11 seccomp, V12 inherited handles, V14 AppImage, V28 hostname, V29 local filesystem, V30 crash artifacts, V32 platform baselines, V33 no tray host). **G-5** is the plan's label for the `RegExpCompiler` question (§9.3 lists `RegExp` only). V14 is added to the findings the task list names, because T12's AppImage smoke job gives evidence for it: the `__cli` half and, through T11's CI-only `--autostart-probe`, the autostart half (the `Exec=` of the entry that `tauri-plugin-autostart` writes inside an AppImage).
- **One recorded commit.** The exit criterion says "on the recorded commit", so the document has one `## Recorded commit` and every row carries the same SHA (the checker enforces it).
- **Two commits, and why.** A document cannot contain its own SHA, and the CI steps that print the per-probe evidence (below) must have run on the recorded commit. So: **commit E** (evidence commit) adds `probe_evidence.rs` and the `ci.yml` evidence steps and job; all three workflows must be green on E; E is the recorded commit. **Commit D** (document commit) adds the checker, its tests, the document and the `ci.yml` check step. D may change only the four files in `ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD`; `--verify-git` checks that. D's own CI run is a gate but is not recorded, because it contains the document.
- **Do not push anything between E and the end of Step 4.** `ci.yml` cancels an older run of the same ref on every new push (`cancel-in-progress` on non-default branches, T02). A second push would cancel the runs that the record needs.
- **Plan addition outside the task's file list: `probe_evidence.rs` and the `ci.yml` steps.** The document needs each floor probe's outcome and evidence code. The `sandbox_probe` log line (T20) carries only `floor`, `failed`, `extra_layers`, `engine_version`, `worker_version` and `ace`, and the T16 to T19 tests assert but do not print per-probe evidence. The new test prints the real startup probe report (T20 `run_startup_probe`). If you do not want a test file for this, the alternative is to cite the assertion text of T17 to T19 instead of the evidence codes; then drop `probe_evidence.rs`, the `Probe evidence` steps and the `probe-evidence-fedora` job and loosen the checker's probe table.
- **Evidence has two sources, and that is stated in the document.** The probe table comes from the dev build (the `cargo test` leg of the target). The installed package is evidenced by its `event=sandbox_probe` line (T21): `floor=met` with an empty `failed=` proves every floor probe was Blocked. One consequence: on macOS the dev-build test binary is not hardened, so its `task_for_pid` probe is `allowed` there. The row takes that probe's `blocked` from the installed hardened app (T21), and the cell says so. No other cell is edited.
- **Verdict rule.** GO if and only if every floor probe is `blocked`, every install line of the row says `floor=met`, and on Linux every worker thread is confined (`all_seccomp_2=true`, `all_no_new_privs_1=true`). Otherwise NO-GO with a reason that names the probe or step. Extra layers (Landlock) never matter. The checker enforces all of it.
- **Fedora row.** The `probe-evidence-fedora` job builds on ubuntu-22.04 (glibc 2.35) and runs the test binary inside `fedora:40` (glibc 2.39) with Docker's default seccomp profile, the way T17 runs its probes. A container shares the runner's kernel, so this proves the glibc half of V11 and not a Fedora kernel. The install line comes from the real rpm install (T21 `fedora-rpm`).
- **GitHub and `gh`.** CI is GitHub Actions (T02). `--verify-runs` calls `gh api` (REST) for run and job data, and the fill script uses `gh run view --job <id> --log`. `gh` must be installed and authenticated. If the project's CI is not GitHub, port the three data calls and keep the format.
- **A human reviews the document.** The `reviewed by` line is filled with the name the user gives. Do not invent one.

**Evidence line grammar** (printed by `probe_evidence.rs`, read by the fill script in Step 8):
```text
RUNNER_FACT <free text>
PROBE_EVIDENCE os=<os> arch=<arch> app_pid=<n> non_dumpable=<Ok(())|Err(..)> ace_ensure_ran=<bool>
PROBE_EVIDENCE worker_version=<Option<String>> engine_version=<Option<String>>
PROBE_EVIDENCE floor=<Met|NotMet { failed: [...] }>
PROBE_EVIDENCE confinement=<Option<ConfinementReport>>
PROBE_EVIDENCE threads=<None|Some(ThreadConfinement { tasks: <n>, all_seccomp_2: <bool>, all_no_new_privs_1: <bool> })>
PROBE_EVIDENCE extra_layers=<[] | [("landlock", true)]>
PROBE_EVIDENCE identity=<Option<SandboxBinaryIdentity>>
PROBE_EVIDENCE probe=<snake_case id> outcome=<blocked|allowed|error> evidence=<Evidence in Debug form>
PROBE_EVIDENCE done records=<n>
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Check the preconditions (read-only)**

Run (Git Bash, in `C:/Code/atlas-duck`):
```bash
cd /c/Code/atlas-duck
git status --short
git remote -v

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the evidence test (`probe_evidence.rs`) and see it fail to exist**

Run: `cargo test -p atlas-duck-app --test probe_evidence --locked`
Expected: FAIL with `error: no test target named `probe_evidence` in `atlas-duck-app` package`.

Create `app/src-tauri/tests/probe_evidence.rs`:
```rust
//! Prints this OS's §9.4 probe report as `PROBE_EVIDENCE` lines, the source of the per-probe
//! table in docs/m1/go-no-go.md (plan task T22).
//!
//! It runs the real startup probe (`sandbox_probe::run_startup_probe`) against the dev-built
//! `atlas-duck-sandbox`, copied into a temporary install directory. The floor verdict is not
//! asserted here: the live assertions are in probes_linux.rs, probes_macos.rs and
//! probes_windows.rs, and the go/no-go record carries the verdict per OS. This test fails only if
//! the probe produced no records at all.
//!
//! Read it with: cargo test -p atlas-duck-app --test probe_evidence --locked -- --nocapture
//!
//! `ATLAS_DUCK_SANDBOX_BIN` overrides the worker (used by the Fedora container job, where the
//! compile-time `CARGO_BIN_EXE_atlas-duck-sandbox` path does not exist).

use std::path::PathBuf;

use atlas_duck_app_lib::sandbox_probe::{run_startup_probe, sandbox_worker_path};
use atlas_duck_app_lib::startup::crash::set_non_dumpable;

fn worker_source() -> PathBuf {
    match std::env::var_os("ATLAS_DUCK_SANDBOX_BIN") {
        Some(path) => PathBuf::from(path),
        None => PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_atlas-duck-sandbox")),
    }
}

/// `FileInProfile` -> `file_in_profile`; the spelling of `ProbeId`'s serde `snake_case`
/// (`Clone3` -> `clone3`), which is what the go/no-go document uses.
fn snake_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (i, c) in name.chars().enumerate() {
        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('_');
            }
            out.push(c.to_ascii_lowercase());
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn snake_case_matches_the_probe_id_spelling() {
    assert_eq!(snake_case("FileInProfile"), "file_in_profile");
    assert_eq!(snake_case("Clone3"), "clone3");
    assert_eq!(snake_case("MemReadProcMem"), "mem_read_proc_mem");
    assert_eq!(snake_case("MachLookupSecurityd"), "mach_lookup_securityd");
    assert_eq!(snake_case("Blocked"), "blocked");
}

#[test]
fn print_probe_evidence() {
    // Linux: the app is non-dumpable (§2.5), which the memory-read probes rely on (§9.4).
    // Other OSes return Unsupported; that is printed, not an error.
    let non_dumpable = set_non_dumpable();

    let install_dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("atlas-duck-probe-evidence-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&install_dir).expect("create the temporary install dir");
    std::fs::copy(worker_source(), sandbox_worker_path(&install_dir)).expect("copy the sandbox worker");

    let profile = std::env::var_os(if cfg!(windows) { "USERPROFILE" } else { "HOME" })
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| install_dir.clone());

    let app_pid = std::process::id();
    let (report, ace) = run_startup_probe(&install_dir, app_pid, &profile);

    println!(
        "PROBE_EVIDENCE os={} arch={} app_pid={app_pid} non_dumpable={non_dumpable:?} ace_ensure_ran={}",
        std::env::consts::OS,
        std::env::consts::ARCH,
        ace.is_some()
    );
    println!(
        "PROBE_EVIDENCE worker_version={:?} engine_version={:?}",
        report.worker_version, report.engine_version
    );
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE floor={:?}", report.floor);
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE confinement={:?}", report.confinement);
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE threads={:?}", report.threads);
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE extra_layers={:?}", report.extra_layers);
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE identity={:?}", report.identity);
    for record in &report.records {
        println!(
            "PROBE_EVIDENCE probe={} outcome={} evidence={:?}",
            snake_case(&format!("{:?}", record.probe)),
            snake_case(&format!("{:?}", record.outcome)),
            record.evidence
        );
    }
    println!("PROBE_EVIDENCE done records={}", report.records.len());

    // Best effort: the worker may still be exiting on Windows.
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&install_dir);

    assert!(!report.records.is_empty(), "the startup probe produced no records");
}
```

```yaml
  probe-evidence-fedora:
    name: probe-evidence-fedora (§9.4 probes on Fedora 40, glibc 2.39)
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Linux system packages (Tauri, tray, D-Bus, Xvfb)
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libdbus-1-dev \
            dbus-x11 \
            xvfb

      - name: Install the pinned Rust toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rustup toolchain install
          rustup show active-toolchain

      - name: Cache cargo registry and target dir
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          key: probe-evidence-fedora
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) }}

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Build the UI (tauri::generate_context! reads app/ui/dist)
        run: |
          npm --prefix app/ui ci --ignore-scripts
          npm --prefix app/ui run build

      - name: Build the probe-evidence test binary and the sandbox worker on ubuntu-22.04
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo build -p atlas-duck-app --bin atlas-duck-sandbox --locked
          cargo test -p atlas-duck-app --test probe_evidence --locked --no-run --message-format=json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/build.json"
          exe="$(node -e '
            const fs = require("fs");
            let exe = "";
            for (const line of fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").split("\n")) {
              let m;
              try { m = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }
              if (m.reason === "compiler-artifact" && m.executable && m.target && m.target.name === "probe_evidence") exe = m.executable;
            }
            console.log(exe);
          ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/build.json")"
          test -x "$exe"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/fedora"
          cp "$exe" "$RUNNER_TEMP/fedora/probe_evidence"
          cp target/debug/atlas-duck-sandbox "$RUNNER_TEMP/fedora/atlas-duck-sandbox"
          ls -l "$RUNNER_TEMP/fedora"

      - name: Probe evidence (§9.4, go/no-go record)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP/fedora:/w:ro" \
            -e ATLAS_DUCK_SANDBOX_BIN=/w/atlas-duck-sandbox \
            fedora:40 sh -c '
              set -e
              echo "RUNNER_FACT $(rpm -q glibc) on kernel $(uname -r)"
              if ! dnf install -y webkit2gtk4.1 libayatana-appindicator-gtk3 > /tmp/dnf.log 2>&1; then
                cat /tmp/dnf.log
                exit 1
              fi
              /w/probe_evidence --nocapture --test-threads=1
            '
```

Notes on the job:
- `docker run` mounts the two binaries read-only into `fedora:40`; the test copies the worker into its own temp "install dir" inside the container, so the read-only mount is fine. `ATLAS_DUCK_SANDBOX_BIN` replaces the compile-time `CARGO_BIN_EXE_atlas-duck-sandbox` path, which does not exist in the container.
- The test binary links WebKitGTK, so the container installs the same two runtime packages as T17 and T12 (`webkit2gtk4.1`, `libayatana-appindicator-gtk3`).
- If Docker's default seccomp profile blocks the `seccomp()` syscall inside the container, the worker's confinement fails and the table shows it. Record that. Do not loosen the floor.

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the failing test for the checker**

Create `ci/check-go-no-go.test.mjs`. The fixture builder `validDoc()` writes a complete synthetic document (test data only, never the real one) and the tests mutate it:
````javascript
// node --test "ci/*.test.mjs"  (node:test, no npm dependencies)
import { test } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import {
  ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD,
  FLOOR_PROBES,
  REQUIRED_FINDINGS,
  REQUIRED_OPEN_ITEMS,
  REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS,
  TARGET_OS,
  check,
  verifyGit,
  verifyRuns,
} from "./check-go-no-go.mjs";

const REPO = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const SHA = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567";
const OTHER_SHA = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98";
const REPO_URL = "https://github.com/example/atlas-duck/actions/runs";
const RUN_IDS = { "ci.yml": 1001, "bundle.yml": 1002, "install-probes.yml": 1003 };

// ----------------------------------------------------------- fixture builder

const jobNames = (file) =>
  REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS[file].map((prefix) => (prefix === "supply-chain" ? "supply-chain (cargo-deny, cargo-audit)" : prefix));

/** A complete, valid document (synthetic data for the checker only). */
function validDoc(over = {}) {
  const o = { sha: SHA, ...over };
  const p = [];
  p.push("# M1 go/no-go record", "", "## Recorded commit", "", `- commit: \`${o.sha}\``, "- recorded on: 2026-10-08", "");
  p.push("## Workflow runs on the recorded commit", "");
  for (const file of Object.keys(REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS)) {
    p.push(`### ${file}`, "", `- run: ${REPO_URL}/${RUN_IDS[file]}`);
    for (const j of jobNames(file)) p.push(`- job: ${j}`);
    p.push("");
  }
  p.push("## Targets", "");
  let n = 0;
  for (const [id, os] of Object.entries(TARGET_OS)) {
    if (o.skipTarget === id) continue;
    n += 1;
    const verdict = o.verdicts?.[id] ?? "GO";
    p.push(`### ${id}`, "");
    p.push(`- commit: \`${o.targetSha?.[id] ?? o.sha}\``);
    p.push(`- run: ${o.runUrl ?? `${REPO_URL}/1003/job/${9000 + n}`}`);
    p.push(`- verdict: ${verdict}`);
    if (o.reasons?.[id] !== undefined) p.push(`- reason: ${o.reasons[id]}`);
    p.push("- extra layers: none");
    p.push("- evidence source: job `rust (...)`, step `Probe evidence`, lines `PROBE_EVIDENCE`");
    p.push(`- install line: \`event=sandbox_probe floor=${verdict === "GO" ? "met" : "not_met"} failed= extra_layers= ace=n/a\``);
    if (os === "linux") p.push("- threads: tasks=1 all_seccomp_2=true all_no_new_privs_1=true");
    p.push("", "| probe | outcome | evidence |", "|---|---|---|");
    for (const probe of FLOOR_PROBES[os]) {
      if (o.dropProbe === probe) continue;
      const outcome = o.outcomes?.[`${id}:${probe}`] ?? "blocked";
      p.push(`| ${probe} | ${outcome} | Reported { os_error: Some(13) } |`);
    }
    p.push("| engine_self_test | allowed | Reported { os_error: None } |", "");
  }
  p.push("## Findings", "");
  for (const id of REQUIRED_FINDINGS) {
    if (o.skipFinding === id) continue;
    p.push(`### ${id} synthetic title`, "", `- status: ${o.findingStatus ?? "verified"}`, "- evidence: job log line `V00 synthetic`", "");
  }
  p.push("## Open for later milestones", "");
  for (const w of REQUIRED_OPEN_ITEMS) if (o.skipOpen !== w) p.push(`- ${w}: later milestone`);
  p.push("");
  return p.join("\n");
}

const run = (...args) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [join(REPO, "ci", "check-go-no-go.mjs"), ...args], { encoding: "utf8" });

function withDoc(text, fn) {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "go-no-go-"));
  const file = join(dir, "go-no-go.md");
  writeFileSync(file, text);
  try {
    return fn(file);
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

const exitOf = (text) => withDoc(text, (f) => run(f));

// --------------------------------------------------------- required behaviour

test("a complete fixture is valid (library and CLI exit 0)", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(check(validDoc()), []);
  const r = withDoc(validDoc(), (f) => run(f));
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stdout + r.stderr);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /^ok: .*\(6 targets\)/);
});

test("a missing macos-x86_64-rosetta row -> exit 1", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({ skipTarget: "macos-x86_64-rosetta" });
  assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("target macos-x86_64-rosetta: row is missing")));
  const r = withDoc(doc, (f) => run(f));
  assert.equal(r.status, 1);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /target macos-x86_64-rosetta: row is missing/);
});

test("a verdict MAYBE -> exit 1", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({ verdicts: { "fedora-40": "MAYBE" } });
  assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("target fedora-40: verdict 'MAYBE'")));
  assert.equal(exitOf(doc).status, 1);
});

test("a NO-GO without a reason -> exit 1", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({ verdicts: { "windows-per-user": "NO-GO" } });
  assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("target windows-per-user: verdict NO-GO needs a non-empty reason")));
  assert.equal(exitOf(doc).status, 1);
  const blank = validDoc({ verdicts: { "windows-per-user": "NO-GO" }, reasons: { "windows-per-user": "" } });
  assert.equal(exitOf(blank).status, 1);
});

test("a SHA that is not 40 hex chars -> exit 1", () => {
  for (const bad of ["0123456789abcdef", `${SHA}0`, SHA.toUpperCase(), SHA.replace("0", "g")]) {
    const doc = validDoc({ targetSha: { "ubuntu-22.04": bad } });
    assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("target ubuntu-22.04: commit")), bad);
    assert.equal(exitOf(doc).status, 1, bad);
  }
  assert.equal(exitOf(validDoc({ sha: "abc" })).status, 1);
});

// ----------------------------------------------------------- further behaviour

test("a NO-GO row with a reason is a valid record (exit 0)", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({
    verdicts: { "macos-arm64": "NO-GO" },
    reasons: { "macos-arm64": "sandbox_init rejected the SBPL profile on macOS 15 (see job log)" },
    outcomes: { "macos-arm64:spawn_process": "allowed" },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(check(doc), []);
  assert.equal(exitOf(doc).status, 0);
});

test("a run URL that is not https -> exit 1", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({ runUrl: "http://ci.example/runs/1" });
  assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("is not an https URL")));
  assert.equal(exitOf(doc).status, 1);
});

test("a row whose commit differs from the recorded commit -> exit 1", () => {
  const doc = validDoc({ targetSha: { "fedora-40": OTHER_SHA } });
  assert.ok(check(doc).some((v) => v.includes("differs from the recorded commit")));
});

test("GO with an allowed floor probe, a missing floor probe or a failed install line -> exit 1", () => {
  const allowed = validDoc({ outcomes: { "ubuntu-22.04:mem_read_proc_mem": "allowed" } });
  assert.ok(check(allowed).some((v) => v.includes("GO but floor probe mem_read_proc_mem is allowed")));

});

test("findings: a missing finding, a bad status and open-item gaps are violations", () => {

  assert.ok(check(validDoc({ skipFinding: "G-5" })).some((v) => v.includes("finding G-5: section")));
  assert.ok(check(validDoc({ findingStatus: "done" })).some((v) => v.includes("status 'done'")));
  assert.ok(check(validDoc({ skipOpen: "musl" })).some((v) => v.includes("no entry mentions 'musl'")));
  assert.ok(check(validDoc({ skipOpen: "V30" })).some((v) => v.includes("no entry mentions 'V30'")));
  assert.ok(check(validDoc({ skipOpen: "crash-report upload" })).some((v) => v.includes("no entry mentions 'crash-report upload'")));

test("headings inside code fences are ignored and fenced key lines are not parsed", () => {

test("CLI usage and read errors exit 2", () => {

function fakeGithub({ headSha = SHA, conclusion = "success", jobs = {}, status = "completed", path = {}, skipped = "" } = {}) {
  return (endpoint) => {
    const m = /^repos\/example\/atlas-duck\/actions\/runs\/(\d+)(\/jobs)?/.exec(endpoint);
    assert.ok(m, `unexpected endpoint ${endpoint}`);
    const file = Object.keys(RUN_IDS).find((f) => String(RUN_IDS[f]) === m[1]);
    if (m[2]) {
      const names = jobs[file] ?? jobNames(file);
      return { jobs: names.map((name, i) => ({ id: m[1] === "1003" ? 9001 + i : 7000 + i, name, conclusion: name === jobs.fail ? "failure" : name === skipped ? "skipped" : "success" })) };
    }
    return { status, conclusion, head_sha: headSha, path: path[file] ?? `.github/workflows/${file}@refs/heads/main` };
  };
}

test("verifyRuns: all green on the recorded commit -> no violations", () => {

});

  assert.ok(verifyRuns(validDoc(), fakeGithub({ jobs: { fail: "bundle-linux" } })).some((v) => v.includes("job 'bundle-linux' concluded failure")));
  assert.ok(
    verifyRuns(validDoc(), fakeGithub({ jobs: { "ci.yml": [...jobNames("ci.yml"), "extra-job"] } })).some((v) => v.includes("has job 'extra-job', the document does not list it")),
  );
  assert.ok(verifyRuns(validDoc(), fakeGithub({ path: { "bundle.yml": ".github/workflows/ci.yml" } })).some((v) => v.includes("belongs to workflow")));

Create `ci/check-go-no-go.mjs`:
````javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Checks docs/m1/go-no-go.md (T22, spec §14 M1: "Ends with a recorded go/no-go per OS").
//
//   node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs docs/m1/go-no-go.md                 static check
//   node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs docs/m1/go-no-go.md --verify-git    + recorded commit is in this history
//   node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs docs/m1/go-no-go.md --verify-runs   + the recorded CI runs are green (needs `gh`)
//
// Exit codes: 0 = ok, 1 = violations (one per line on stdout), 2 = usage or unreadable file.
// A NO-GO row is a valid record and passes the static check. The M1 exit criterion
// (every workflow green on the recorded commit) is the separate --verify-runs mode.
// No npm dependencies.

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- constants

/** Floor probe ids per OS, in the serde snake_case spelling of `ProbeId` (T13). */
export const FLOOR_PROBES = {
  windows: [
    "file_in_profile",
    "connect_loopback",
    "connect_public",
    "spawn_process",
    "open_process_vm_read",
    "cred_read",
    "open_clipboard",
  ],
  macos: [
    "file_in_profile",
    "connect_loopback",
    "connect_public",
    "spawn_process",
    "task_for_pid",
    "mach_lookup_securityd",
  ],
  linux: [
    "file_in_profile",
    "connect_loopback",
    "connect_public",
    "spawn_process",
    "raw_clone",
    "clone3",
    "mem_read_process_vm",
    "mem_read_proc_mem",
  ],
};

/** Diagnostic probes (never part of the floor, T13 `ProbeId::is_floor`). */
export const DIAGNOSTIC_PROBES = ["engine_self_test", "env_names", "handle_sentinel"];

/** Required targets (T22 produces list) and the OS whose floor list applies. */
export const TARGET_OS = {
  "windows-per-user": "windows",
  "windows-per-machine": "windows",
  "macos-arm64": "macos",
  "macos-x86_64-rosetta": "macos",
  "ubuntu-22.04": "linux",
  "fedora-40": "linux",
};

export const OUTCOMES = ["blocked", "allowed", "error"];
export const VERDICTS = ["GO", "NO-GO"];
export const FINDING_STATUSES = ["verified", "partial", "open"];

/** §15 verify items M1 produced findings for (V numbers count the §15 bullets from V01; G-5 is the plan's RegExpCompiler gap). */
export const REQUIRED_FINDINGS = [
  "V02",
  "G-5",
  "V03",
  "V09",
  "V10",
  "V11",
  "V12",
  "V14",
  "V28",
  "V29",
  "V30",
  "V32",
  "V33",
];

/**
 * Words that must appear in the "Open for later milestones" section. "V30" and "crash-report upload"
 * keep the unresolved WebView2 requirement of §2.5 / §15 V30 in the record (review issue: it must not drop out).
 */
export const REQUIRED_OPEN_ITEMS = ["watchdog", "degraded", "musl", "native Intel", "APP_START", "Settings", "V30", "crash-report upload"];

/** Workflows and the job names (prefix match, case-insensitive) each run must list. */
export const REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS = {
  "ci.yml": [
    "rust (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)",
    "rust (aarch64-apple-darwin)",
    "rust (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)",
    "rust (x86_64-apple-darwin under Rosetta)",
    "supply-chain",
    "ui",
    "locality-mounts",
    "probe-evidence-fedora",
  ],
  "bundle.yml": [
    "bundle-windows",
    "bundle-macos-arm64",
    "bundle-macos-x86_64",
    "bundle-linux",
    "fedora-rpm",
    "appimage-smoke",
  ],
  "install-probes.yml": [
    "windows-per-user",
    "windows-per-machine",
    "macos-arm64",
    "macos-x86_64-rosetta",
    "ubuntu-deb",
    "ubuntu-appimage",
    "fedora-rpm",
  ],
};

/** Files a commit after the recorded commit may change (the T22 commit). */
export const ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD = [
  "docs/m1/go-no-go.md",
  "ci/check-go-no-go.mjs",
  "ci/check-go-no-go.test.mjs",
  ".github/workflows/ci.yml",
];

const SHA_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;
const HTTPS_RE = /^https:\/\/[^\s/]+\/\S+$/;
const GITHUB_RUN_RE = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/\s]+)\/([^/\s]+)\/actions\/runs\/(\d+)(?:\/job\/(\d+))?$/;
const UNFILLED_RE = /@@FILL|\bTBD\b|\bTODO\b|\bFIXME\b/;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing

/**
 * Splits the document into sections at `##` and `###` headings. Headings inside
 * fenced code blocks are ignored, and fenced lines are not parsed as key/value
 * lines or table rows.
 */
export function parseSections(text) {
  const sections = [];
  let current = { level: 0, title: "", parent: "", lines: [] };
  let h2 = "";
  let inFence = false;
  sections.push(current);
  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    if (/^\s*```/.test(line)) {
      inFence = !inFence;
      continue;
    }
    if (inFence) continue;
    const m = /^(##|###) +(.+?) *$/.exec(line);
    if (m) {
      const level = m[1].length;
      if (level === 2) h2 = m[2];
      current = { level, title: m[2], parent: level === 2 ? "" : h2, lines: [] };
      sections.push(current);
      continue;
    }
    current.lines.push(line);
  }
  return sections;
}

const unquote = (s) => s.trim().replace(/^`([^`]*)`$/, "$1").trim();

/** `- key: value` lines of a section as { key: [values...] } (keys lower-case). */
export function keyValues(section) {
  const out = {};
  for (const line of section.lines) {
    const m = /^- ([a-z][a-z ]*?):[ \t]*(.*)$/.exec(line);
    if (!m) continue;
    (out[m[1]] ??= []).push(unquote(m[2]));
  }
  return out;
}

/** Table rows (after the header and separator) as arrays of trimmed cells. */
export function tableRows(section) {
  const rows = [];
  for (const line of section.lines) {
    if (!/^\s*\|/.test(line)) continue;
    const cells = line
      .trim()
      .replace(/^\|/, "")
      .replace(/\|$/, "")
      .split("|")
      .map((c) => c.trim());
    if (cells.every((c) => /^:?-{3,}:?$/.test(c))) continue;
    rows.push(cells);
  }
  return rows.slice(1); // the header row
}

const one = (kv, key) => (kv[key] ?? [])[0] ?? "";

// ------------------------------------------------------------------- checks

function checkRecordedCommit(sections, out) {
  const sec = sections.find((s) => s.level === 2 && s.title === "Recorded commit");
  if (!sec) {
    out.push("recorded commit: section '## Recorded commit' is missing");
    return "";
  }
  const sha = one(keyValues(sec), "commit");
  if (!SHA_RE.test(sha)) {
    out.push(`recorded commit: '${sha}' is not 40 lower-case hex characters`);
    return "";
  }
  return sha;
}

function checkWorkflows(sections, out) {
  for (const [file, required] of Object.entries(REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS)) {
    const sec = sections.find((s) => s.level === 3 && s.title === file);
    if (!sec) {
      out.push(`workflow ${file}: section '### ${file}' is missing`);
      continue;
    }
    const kv = keyValues(sec);
    const run = one(kv, "run");
    if (!HTTPS_RE.test(run)) out.push(`workflow ${file}: run '${run}' is not an https URL`);
    for (const prefix of required) {
      const found = (kv.job ?? []).some((j) => j.toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix.toLowerCase()));
      if (!found) out.push(`workflow ${file}: no job named '${prefix}...' is listed`);
    }
  }
}

function checkTarget(id, os, sec, recorded, out) {
  const at = `target ${id}`;
  const kv = keyValues(sec);

  const sha = one(kv, "commit");
  if (!SHA_RE.test(sha)) out.push(`${at}: commit '${sha}' is not 40 lower-case hex characters`);
  else if (recorded && sha !== recorded) out.push(`${at}: commit ${sha} differs from the recorded commit ${recorded}`);

  const run = one(kv, "run");
  if (!HTTPS_RE.test(run)) out.push(`${at}: run '${run}' is not an https URL`);

  const verdict = one(kv, "verdict");
  if (!VERDICTS.includes(verdict)) out.push(`${at}: verdict '${verdict}' is not one of ${VERDICTS.join(", ")}`);
  if (verdict === "NO-GO" && one(kv, "reason") === "") out.push(`${at}: verdict NO-GO needs a non-empty reason`);

  if (one(kv, "extra layers") === "") out.push(`${at}: 'extra layers' is empty (write 'none' if there are none)`);
  if (one(kv, "evidence source") === "") out.push(`${at}: 'evidence source' is empty`);

  const lines = kv["install line"] ?? [];
  if (lines.length === 0) out.push(`${at}: no 'install line' (the event=sandbox_probe line of the install job)`);
  for (const l of lines) {
    if (!l.includes("event=sandbox_probe")) out.push(`${at}: install line lacks event=sandbox_probe: ${l}`);
    else if (verdict === "GO" && !/(^|\s)floor=met(\s|$)/.test(l)) out.push(`${at}: GO but install line is not floor=met: ${l}`);
  }

  if (os === "linux") {
    const threads = one(kv, "threads");
    if (threads === "") out.push(`${at}: Linux row needs 'threads' (every worker thread Seccomp: 2 and NoNewPrivs: 1, §9.4)`);
    else if (verdict === "GO" && !(/all_seccomp_2=true/.test(threads) && /all_no_new_privs_1=true/.test(threads)))
      out.push(`${at}: GO but threads is not all_seccomp_2=true and all_no_new_privs_1=true: ${threads}`);
  }

  const seen = new Map();
  for (const row of tableRows(sec)) {
    const probe = unquote(row[0] ?? "");
    const outcome = unquote(row[1] ?? "");
    const evidence = (row[2] ?? "").trim();
    if (seen.has(probe)) out.push(`${at}: probe ${probe} is listed twice`);
    seen.set(probe, outcome);
    if (!FLOOR_PROBES[os].includes(probe) && !DIAGNOSTIC_PROBES.includes(probe)) out.push(`${at}: unknown probe '${probe}' for ${os}`);
    if (!OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) out.push(`${at}: probe ${probe} outcome '${outcome}' is not one of ${OUTCOMES.join(", ")}`);
    if (evidence === "") out.push(`${at}: probe ${probe} has no evidence`);
  }
  for (const probe of FLOOR_PROBES[os]) {
    if (!seen.has(probe)) out.push(`${at}: floor probe ${probe} is missing from the probe table`);
    else if (verdict === "GO" && seen.get(probe) !== "blocked") out.push(`${at}: GO but floor probe ${probe} is ${seen.get(probe)}`);
  }
}

function checkFindings(sections, out) {
  for (const id of REQUIRED_FINDINGS) {
    const sec = sections.find((s) => s.level === 3 && s.parent === "Findings" && (s.title === id || s.title.startsWith(`${id} `)));
    if (!sec) {
      out.push(`finding ${id}: section '### ${id} ...' under '## Findings' is missing`);
      continue;
    }
    const kv = keyValues(sec);
    const status = one(kv, "status");
    if (!FINDING_STATUSES.includes(status)) out.push(`finding ${id}: status '${status}' is not one of ${FINDING_STATUSES.join(", ")}`);
    if (one(kv, "evidence") === "") out.push(`finding ${id}: 'evidence' is empty`);
  }
}

function checkOpenItems(sections, out) {
  const sec = sections.find((s) => s.level === 2 && s.title === "Open for later milestones");
  if (!sec) {
    out.push("open items: section '## Open for later milestones' is missing");
    return;
  }
  const body = sec.lines.join("\n").toLowerCase();
  for (const word of REQUIRED_OPEN_ITEMS) {
    if (!body.includes(word.toLowerCase())) out.push(`open items: no entry mentions '${word}'`);
  }
}

/** Static check. Returns the violations, one string each; [] means the document is valid. */
export function check(text) {
  const out = [];
  text.split(/\r?\n/).forEach((line, i) => {
    if (UNFILLED_RE.test(line)) out.push(`line ${i + 1}: unfilled marker (@@FILL, TBD, TODO or FIXME): ${line.trim()}`);
  });
  const sections = parseSections(text);
  const recorded = checkRecordedCommit(sections, out);
  checkWorkflows(sections, out);
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const sec of sections.filter((s) => s.level === 3 && s.parent === "Targets")) {
    if (!(sec.title in TARGET_OS)) {
      out.push(`target ${sec.title}: not a known target (${Object.keys(TARGET_OS).join(", ")})`);
      continue;
    }
    if (seen.has(sec.title)) out.push(`target ${sec.title}: listed twice`);
    seen.add(sec.title);
    checkTarget(sec.title, TARGET_OS[sec.title], sec, recorded, out);
  }
  for (const id of Object.keys(TARGET_OS)) {
    if (!seen.has(id)) out.push(`target ${id}: row is missing (expected '### ${id}' under '## Targets')`);
  }
  checkFindings(sections, out);
  checkOpenItems(sections, out);
  return out;
}

// ------------------------------------------------- exit-criterion verification

/** The recorded commit, workflow runs and per-target run URLs of a statically valid document. */
function recordedFacts(text) {
  const sections = parseSections(text);
  const sec = sections.find((s) => s.level === 2 && s.title === "Recorded commit");
  const commit = sec ? one(keyValues(sec), "commit") : "";
  const runs = {};
  for (const file of Object.keys(REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS)) {
    const w = sections.find((s) => s.level === 3 && s.title === file);
    if (w) {
      const kv = keyValues(w);
      runs[file] = { run: one(kv, "run"), jobs: kv.job ?? [] };
    }
  }
  const rows = {};
  for (const id of Object.keys(TARGET_OS)) {
    const t = sections.find((s) => s.level === 3 && s.parent === "Targets" && s.title === id);
    if (t) rows[id] = one(keyValues(t), "run");
  }
  return { commit, runs, rows };
}

/**
 * M1 exit criterion: on the recorded commit every listed workflow run is
 * completed and successful, ran that commit, ran exactly the listed jobs, and
 * every job succeeded. `fetchJson(endpoint)` is `gh api <endpoint>` in the CLI.
 */
export function verifyRuns(text, fetchJson) {
  const out = [];
  const { commit, runs, rows } = recordedFacts(text);
  const runIds = {};
  for (const [file, { run, jobs: listed }] of Object.entries(runs)) {
    const m = GITHUB_RUN_RE.exec(run);
    if (!m) {
      out.push(`runs ${file}: '${run}' is not a github.com .../actions/runs/<id> URL`);
      continue;
    }
    const [, owner, repo, id] = m;
    runIds[file] = { id, jobIds: new Set() };
    const base = `repos/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${id}`;
    const info = fetchJson(base);
    if (info.status !== "completed" || info.conclusion !== "success") out.push(`runs ${file}: run ${id} is ${info.status}/${info.conclusion}, expected completed/success`);
    if (info.head_sha !== commit) out.push(`runs ${file}: run ${id} ran ${info.head_sha}, the recorded commit is ${commit}`);
    const wfPath = String(info.path ?? "").split("@")[0];
    if (wfPath !== `.github/workflows/${file}`) out.push(`runs ${file}: run ${id} belongs to workflow '${wfPath}'`);
    const jobs = fetchJson(`${base}/jobs?per_page=100`).jobs ?? [];
    for (const j of jobs) {
      runIds[file].jobIds.add(String(j.id));
      // A skipped job outside the required list is fine; a required job must have run and succeeded.
      const required = REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS[file].some((prefix) => j.name.toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix.toLowerCase()));
      const ok = j.conclusion === "success" || (j.conclusion === "skipped" && !required);
      if (!ok) out.push(`runs ${file}: job '${j.name}' concluded ${j.conclusion}`);
    }
    const actual = new Set(jobs.map((j) => j.name));
    for (const name of listed) if (!actual.has(name)) out.push(`runs ${file}: the document lists job '${name}', the run has no such job`);
    for (const name of actual) if (!listed.includes(name)) out.push(`runs ${file}: the run has job '${name}', the document does not list it`);
  }
  const probes = runIds["install-probes.yml"];
  for (const [id, run] of Object.entries(rows)) {
    const m = GITHUB_RUN_RE.exec(run);
    if (!m) {
      out.push(`runs target ${id}: '${run}' is not a github.com .../actions/runs/<id>[/job/<id>] URL`);
      continue;
    }
    if (probes && m[3] !== probes.id) out.push(`runs target ${id}: run ${m[3]} is not the install-probes.yml run ${probes.id}`);
    if (probes && m[4] && !probes.jobIds.has(m[4])) out.push(`runs target ${id}: job ${m[4]} is not a job of run ${probes.id}`);
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The recorded commit exists, is an ancestor of HEAD, and HEAD differs from it
 * only in the T22 files. `git(args)` returns stdout and throws on a non-zero exit.
 */
export function verifyGit(text, git) {
  const out = [];
  const { commit } = recordedFacts(text);
  try {
    git(["cat-file", "-e", `${commit}^{commit}`]);
  } catch {
    return [`git: commit ${commit} does not exist in this repository (fetch full history)`];
  }
  try {
    git(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, "HEAD"]);
  } catch {
    out.push(`git: recorded commit ${commit} is not an ancestor of HEAD`);
    return out;
  }
  const changed = git(["diff", "--name-only", commit, "HEAD"]).split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean);
  for (const f of changed) {
    if (!ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD.includes(f)) out.push(`git: ${f} changed after the recorded commit; only ${ALLOWED_AFTER_RECORD.join(", ")} may`);
  }
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI

function runCli(argv) {
  const flags = argv.filter((a) => a.startsWith("--"));
  const paths = argv.filter((a) => !a.startsWith("--"));
  const known = ["--verify-git", "--verify-runs"];
  if (paths.length !== 1 || flags.some((f) => !known.includes(f))) {
    console.error("usage: node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs <go-no-go.md> [--verify-git] [--verify-runs]");
    return 2;
  }
  let text;
  try {
    text = readFileSync(paths[0], "utf8");
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`cannot read ${paths[0]}: ${e.code ?? e.message}`);
    return 2;
  }
  const violations = check(text);
  if (violations.length === 0 && flags.includes("--verify-git")) {
    const git = (args) => {
      const r = spawnSync("git", args, { encoding: "utf8" });
      if (r.error || r.status !== 0) throw new Error(r.stderr || String(r.error));
      return r.stdout;
    };
    violations.push(...verifyGit(text, git));
  }
  if (violations.length === 0 && flags.includes("--verify-runs")) {
    const fetchJson = (endpoint) => {
      const r = spawnSync("gh", ["api", endpoint], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
      if (r.error || r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`gh api ${endpoint} failed: ${r.stderr || r.error}`);
      return JSON.parse(r.stdout);
    };
    try {
      violations.push(...verifyRuns(text, fetchJson));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(String(e.message ?? e));
      return 2;
    }
  }
  for (const v of violations) console.log(v);
  if (violations.length > 0) return 1;
  console.log(`ok: ${paths[0]} (${Object.keys(TARGET_OS).length} targets${flags.length ? ", " + flags.join(" ") : ""})`);
  return 0;
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  process.exitCode = runCli(process.argv.slice(2));
}
````

```markdown
# M1 go/no-go record

Spec §14 M1 ends with "a recorded go/no-go per OS". This file is that record. The spec does not say where to record it (plan gap G2); the plan chose this file. `node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs docs/m1/go-no-go.md` checks its shape and runs in the `rust` job. `node ci/check-go-no-go.mjs docs/m1/go-no-go.md --verify-git --verify-runs` checks it against git and GitHub (the M1 exit criterion).

## How to read a verdict

- GO: on this target the §9.4 floor is applied and verified. Every floor probe is `blocked`, every `event=sandbox_probe` line of the target's install job says `floor=met`, and on Linux every worker thread shows `Seccomp: 2` and `NoNewPrivs: 1`.
- NO-GO: anything else. The `reason` line names the failing probe or step and where its evidence is.
- Runtime meaning of a NO-GO (fixed by §9.4): scripts are disabled on that OS (`failed`, exit 8, `error.code = sandbox_unavailable`) unless the user enables "Allow scripts with degraded confinement". What a NO-GO means for the project (for example whether to try the `-gnu` Windows toolchain, research A1) is the user's decision and is not made here.
- Extra layers (Landlock) are reported and never change a verdict (§9.4).
- Evidence has two sources. The per-probe table comes from the dev build: the `cargo test` leg of the target, step `Probe evidence (§9.4, go/no-go record)`, lines starting with `PROBE_EVIDENCE`. The installed package is evidenced by its `event=sandbox_probe` line from the install-probes job. That line carries only `floor`, `failed`, `extra_layers`, `engine_version`, `worker_version` and `ace`, so it proves the floor probes by `floor=met` with an empty `failed=`. On macOS the dev-build test binary is not hardened, so its `task_for_pid` probe is expected to be `allowed` there. The installed hardened app is the evidence for that one probe.

M6 replaces it with the real Settings enable path or keeps it behind the same two guards. What the plugin writes on macOS (LaunchAgent or AppleScript login item) and Windows (Run key) was not observed in M1: only the Linux AppImage case is probed.
- NSIS upgrade drain, "delete app data" disabled and the uninstall checks are M10. A successful script run with degraded confinement off is M8.

- [ ] **Step 9: Fill in the document from the CI logs of commit E**

9a. Run the fill script. It reads the runs of E from GitHub, lists their jobs, pulls each target's `PROBE_EVIDENCE` lines from the dev-build job and each install line from the install-probes job, and splices them into the skeleton. Keep the shell open afterwards: it defines `log_of`, `jobs_of`, `q` and the run ids for Step 9d. Fragments go to a temp dir, not into the repo.
````bash
cd /c/Code/atlas-duck
FILL="$(mktemp -d)/fill.sh"
cat > "$FILL" <<'FILL_SCRIPT'
# Fills docs/m1/go-no-go.md from the CI runs of the recorded commit. Run it with `source`.
# Needs: SHA (recorded commit), gh (authenticated), node, GNU sed (Git Bash).
DOC=docs/m1/go-no-go.md
REPO="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner)"
OUT="$(mktemp -d)"
echo "fragments (not part of the repo): $OUT"
MISSING=0

cat > "$OUT/q.mjs" <<'EOF'
// q.mjs <command> [argument]: reads a GitHub REST JSON document from stdin.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const [cmd, arg] = process.argv.slice(2);
const data = JSON.parse(readFileSync(0, "utf8"));
const jobs = data.jobs ?? [];
const runs = (data.workflow_runs ?? [])
  .filter((r) => String(r.path).split("@")[0] === `.github/workflows/${arg}` && r.status === "completed")
  .sort((a, b) => String(a.run_started_at).localeCompare(String(b.run_started_at)));
const job = jobs.find((j) => j.name.startsWith(arg ?? "\u0000"));
const fail = (m) => { console.error(m); process.exit(1); };
switch (cmd) {
  case "run-id": runs.length ? console.log(runs.at(-1).id) : fail(`no completed run of ${arg}`); break;
  case "run-url": runs.length ? console.log(runs.at(-1).html_url) : fail(`no completed run of ${arg}`); break;
  case "job-id": job ? console.log(job.id) : fail(`no job named ${arg}...`); break;
  case "job-url": job ? console.log(job.html_url) : fail(`no job named ${arg}...`); break;
  case "job-lines": jobs.forEach((j) => console.log(`- job: ${j.name}`)); break;
  default: fail(`unknown command ${cmd}`);
}
EOF
q() { node "$OUT/q.mjs" "$@"; }
jobs_of() { gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$1/jobs?per_page=100"; }
log_of() { gh run view --repo "$REPO" --job "$(jobs_of "$1" | q job-id "$2")" --log | tr -d '\r'; }
need() { [ -s "$1" ] || { echo "MISSING: $1" >&2; MISSING=1; }; }

RUNS_JSON="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=100")"
CI_RUN="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-id ci.yml)"
BUNDLE_RUN="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-id bundle.yml)"
PROBES_RUN="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-id install-probes.yml)"
CI_URL="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-url ci.yml)"
BUNDLE_URL="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-url bundle.yml)"
PROBES_URL="$(echo "$RUNS_JSON" | q run-url install-probes.yml)"
echo "runs: ci=$CI_RUN bundle=$BUNDLE_RUN install-probes=$PROBES_RUN"

splice() { sed -i -e "/@@FILL($1)@@/{r $2" -e 'd}' "$DOC"; }
setv() { sed -i "s#@@FILL($1)@@#$2#g" "$DOC"; }

setv commit "$SHA"
setv run-url:ci.yml "$CI_URL"
setv run-url:bundle.yml "$BUNDLE_URL"
setv run-url:install-probes.yml "$PROBES_URL"
for pair in "ci.yml:$CI_RUN" "bundle.yml:$BUNDLE_RUN" "install-probes.yml:$PROBES_RUN"; do
  jobs_of "${pair#*:}" | q job-lines > "$OUT/jobs-${pair%%:*}.md"
  need "$OUT/jobs-${pair%%:*}.md"
  splice "jobs:${pair%%:*}" "$OUT/jobs-${pair%%:*}.md"
done

# frag <target> <job of ci.yml that ran the dump> <install-probes job>...
frag() {
  local t="$1" devjob="$2" d; shift 2
  d="$OUT/$t"; mkdir -p "$d"
  log_of "$CI_RUN" "$devjob" | grep -o 'RUNNER_FACT .*\|PROBE_EVIDENCE .*' > "$d/dev.txt"
  grep '^PROBE_EVIDENCE probe=' "$d/dev.txt" \
    | sed -E 's/^PROBE_EVIDENCE probe=([a-z0-9_]+) outcome=([a-z_]+) evidence=(.*)$/| \1 | \2 | \3 |/' > "$d/probe-rows.md"
  need "$d/probe-rows.md"
  x="$(sed -n 's/^PROBE_EVIDENCE extra_layers=//p' "$d/dev.txt" | head -n 1)"
  [ "$x" = "[]" ] && x=none
  echo "- extra layers: $x" > "$d/extra-layers.md"
  sed -nE 's/^PROBE_EVIDENCE threads=Some\(ThreadConfinement \{ (.*) \}\)$/\1/p' "$d/dev.txt" \
    | sed -E 's/: /=/g; s/,//g; s/^/- threads: /' > "$d/threads.md"
  : > "$d/install-lines.md"
  for ij in "$@"; do
    log_of "$PROBES_RUN" "$ij" > "$d/install-$ij.log"
    grep -o 'event=sandbox_probe.*' "$d/install-$ij.log" | head -n 1 | sed 's/^/- install line: /' >> "$d/install-lines.md"
    # Windows only: icacls and WER lines of the install job
    if grep -qE 'S-1-15-2-[12]|ExcludedApplications' "$d/install-$ij.log"; then
      { echo '- installer evidence (icacls and WER lines of the install job log):'; echo '```text'
        grep -E 'S-1-15-2-[12]|ExcludedApplications|atlas-duck-(app|sandbox)\.exe +REG_DWORD' "$d/install-$ij.log" | sed -E 's/^[^ ]+\t[^\t]+\t[^ ]+ //'
        echo '```'; } > "$d/installer-lines.md"
    fi
  done
  need "$d/install-lines.md"
  setv "job-url:$t" "$(jobs_of "$PROBES_RUN" | q job-url "$1")"
  splice "extra-layers:$t" "$d/extra-layers.md"
  splice "install-lines:$t" "$d/install-lines.md"
  splice "probe-rows:$t" "$d/probe-rows.md"
  [ -s "$d/threads.md" ] && splice "threads:$t" "$d/threads.md"
  [ -s "$d/installer-lines.md" ] && splice "installer-lines:$t" "$d/installer-lines.md"
}
frag windows-per-user       "rust (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)"            windows-per-user
frag windows-per-machine    "rust (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)"            windows-per-machine
frag macos-arm64            "rust (aarch64-apple-darwin)"              macos-arm64
frag macos-x86_64-rosetta   "rust (x86_64-apple-darwin under Rosetta)" macos-x86_64-rosetta
frag ubuntu-22.04           "rust (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)"          ubuntu-deb ubuntu-appimage
frag fedora-40              "probe-evidence-fedora"                    fedora-rpm
echo "MISSING=$MISSING (1 = a fragment above is empty: stop and read the job log)"
grep -c '@@FILL' "$DOC" | sed 's/^/markers left in the document: /'
FILL_SCRIPT
SHA=<the recorded commit E from Step 5>
source "$FILL"
````
